sentiment: Resilience is not one strong thing but many small ones, each carrying a little, none allowed to fail at once.

stories.title: So you think you could be an electrician?
stories.summary: A trade that keeps everything else running, built out of unglamorous competence rather than invention. The knowledge lives in hands and patience — the kind of reliability that only shows up on the day the power goes out.

stories.title: Why don't more developers "use the platform"?
stories.summary: The browser already ships enormous capability, yet we keep rebuilding it in pieces. The platform endures because it is many small, boring, widely-supported parts — a distributed resilience that novelty can't match.

stories.title: In Ukraine, distributed renewables foil Russia's assaults
stories.summary: When the grid is a target, many small sources become the answer: no single node worth destroying, no single failure that spreads. Resilience as redundancy, spread thin on purpose.
